goal: Clarify the flow-plan draft-phase instruction so every user-facing question, including confirmation after applying user-requested changes, must use the Choice Format with no exceptions.

in: Update wording in `src/templates/skills/sdd-forge.flow-plan/SKILL.md` to remove exception-prone phrasing.
Ensure the wording explicitly covers reactive confirmation questions.
Update/add tests that validate the strict wording requirement.
out: Extending the same wording change to `flow-impl` and `flow-finalize`.
Running `sdd-forge build` and regenerating project docs in this spec.
Any runtime behavior changes outside the flow-plan skill template content and its tests.

acceptance_criteria: `src/templates/skills/sdd-forge.flow-plan/SKILL.md` contains strict wording equivalent to: every user question (including post-change confirmations) must use Choice Format; no free-form questions; no exceptions.
Relevant unit tests in the repository assert this strict wording behavior and pass after updates.
No unrelated skill template is modified by this spec.

clarifications.q: Should this spec include docs regeneration work because source is newer than docs?
clarifications.a: No. Keep this spec focused on wording and tests; docs refresh is a separate task.

clarifications.q: Should the strict rule be expanded to other skills now?
clarifications.a: No. Keep this issue scoped to flow-plan only.
Strict MUST wording with explicit confirmation coverage, plus tests to prevent regression.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep current wording (`as default`) and add examples only.
alternatives_considered.reason: Rejected: still allows interpretation drift and exception behavior.

alternatives_considered.option: Apply strict wording to all flow skills in one change.
alternatives_considered.reason: Rejected: violates single-responsibility scope for this issue.
